audits.claim: The newly added Salesforce credential update references an unimported prisma global and fails in production after a successful token refresh.
audits.evidence: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:1-20 contains no prisma import, and its constructor starts getClient at line 57. With NODE_ENV=production, configured Salesforce app keys and a refresh response with statusText OK satisfying the schema at lines 39-47, execution reaches the unbound prisma reference at line 96 and rejects the connection promise with ReferenceError before constructing jsforce.Connection at line 101. packages/prisma/index.ts:6-9 only declares a TypeScript global; its runtime assignment at lines 58-59 is explicitly skipped in production. The prisma import in packages/app-store/_utils/getAppKeysFromSlug.ts:3-6 is local to that module and cannot supply the missing binding; callers awaiting this.conn, such as CalendarService.ts:136-137, consequently fail.

audits.claim: The credential webhook compares its shared secret using ordinary string inequality instead of a constant-time comparison.
audits.evidence: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-28 does use !==, so constant-time comparison would be security hardening, but the repository does not establish an observable timing oracle or a concrete secret-recovery path. The proposed missing-header and array checks already fail closed: packages/lib/constants.ts:103-104 and app-credential.ts:19-20 require a nonempty secret and encryption key, and undefined or an array cannot strictly equal that secret string at lines 25-26. Even after successful secret authentication, writes at lines 73-89 require ciphertext that passes symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse at lines 57-59 using the separately configured encryption key (packages/lib/crypto.ts:32-39). Thus the comparison concern is valid as hardening, but the stated code does not demonstrate an authentication bypass or unauthorized credential overwrite.
